profile.name: Kranthi Kumar Elupula
profile.title: AI Engineer / Software Engineer
profile.headline: AI Engineer building multi-agent systems, RAG pipelines, and production backends — LangGraph, pgvector, and GPU inference that hold up under real traffic.
profile.summary: At Cloud Nest IT I own planning and memory agents in a five-agent financial advisory platform on LangGraph, with RAG over ~50k compliance PDFs, LoRA model routing, and PII/DLP guards in front of ~200 advisors. Before that I shipped data platforms at Aviva, Amazon (AWS HoneyCode), and Cyient. MS Computer Science, Texas A&M–Corpus Christi.

bullets: Own the Planning Agent and Redis-backed Memory Agent in a five-agent financial advisory platform on LangGraph — conditional gates route advisor queries so simple lookups skip expensive reasoning agents.

Built the RAG pipeline: chunked ~50k compliance PDFs into overlapping 512-token segments, embedded them with sentence-transformers into pgvector, and added BM25 reranking — retrieval latency from 12s to under 3s with a RAGAS faithfulness score of 0.91.
Trained a LoRA routing classifier (PyTorch, Hugging Face) that sends simple lookups to a smaller LLM and complex reasoning to GPT-4o, cutting monthly inference cost by 30% across ~10k daily requests.
Added a PII-masking and DLP layer (regex + NER + Pydantic) between agents and the API — rejected 4% of raw LLM outputs with hallucinated or sensitive data before they reached ~200 advisors.
Instrumented all five agents with OpenTelemetry (span per tool call and LLM call) and Prometheus token/latency p95/p99 counters, plus RAGAS + pytest trace replay in CI on every GitHub PR.
Built policy and claims APIs: 8 FastAPI endpoints and 3 in Node.js, serving 30+ underwriters who previously waited 2–3 hours — responses now under 200ms.
Replaced a nightly CSV-over-SFTP batch with a GraphQL layer so two downstream reporting systems received claims updates in near real time instead of 24 hours behind.
Redesigned PostgreSQL (14 tables, 6 views), added composite indexes, and introduced PgBouncer — p95 query time from 800ms to 120ms during peak connection exhaustion.
Containerized 11 microservices in Docker and deployed on Kubernetes with liveness probes and rolling updates, ending staging/prod config-mismatch crashes.
Worked on the AWS HoneyCode platform team (Python, Java) — fixed a critical memory leak that caused 3–4 OOM crashes a week and brought uptime to 99.9%.
Built ETL on AWS (S3 → Glue → Redshift) extracting ~500k usage and billing records per month across 8 source feeds, with deduplication and schema normalization.
Replaced cron triggers with Lambda on S3 events and 15+ CloudWatch alarms — failure detection from next-morning to under 5 minutes.
Migrated a single-threaded ingestion script to Kafka (6 topics, 18 partitions) and Spark on a 5-node EMR cluster with DLQs — throughput from ~2k to ~50k records/hour.
Replaced weekly hand-pasted CSVs with Python ETL from 6 Oracle tables and dumps — ~200k records validated and loaded in under 40 minutes.
Built 8 Flask REST endpoints for an inspection portal and brought p95 from 4+ seconds to under 200ms at ~2k requests/day with pagination and index tuning.
Migrated FTP uploads to Azure Data Factory (Oracle → Azure SQL → PostgreSQL) with schema-drift detection so new source columns did not silently break loads.
Shipped 3 Tableau dashboards for inspection rates, defect trends, and SLA compliance, replacing a Friday spreadsheet that took project managers a full day.

projects.title: Mini vLLM
projects.description: Toy LLM serving engine in llm-lab: baseline GPU throughput, torch.compile, and batching on Qwen2.5, then a paged KV-cache allocator and continuous-batching scheduler with CUDA kernels — validated against PyTorch.
points: Paged KV cache and continuous batching to keep the GPU busy
Baseline benches: single-sequence, compile warmup, batch size, D2D bandwidth
Outputs checked against a PyTorch reference path

projects.title: Financial Multi-Agent System
projects.description: Production-style fintech agents with no paid APIs: text-to-SQL, RAG over policy docs, DLP/PII masking, Kafka routing, Redis caching, and Prometheus/Grafana — local via Ollama, Qdrant, and Docker.
points: Orchestrator routes intents onto Kafka topics + DLQ
SELECT-only SQL, row-level security, output masking

projects.title: GPU Inference Lab
projects.description: Full climb of the GPU inference stack on an RTX 4050 6GB: tokenization, KV cache, CUDA/Triton kernels, AWQ, then vLLM, Ray Serve, and TensorRT-LLM. Measured ~301 tok/s aggregate offline with vLLM 0.23.

projects.title: Kafka Redis Flow
projects.description: End-to-end orders pipeline: Kafka → Redis, Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, and Loki. Lab scenario injects 10k transactions, watches lag and backpressure, then scales workers.

projects.title: LLM Panel Interview Simulator
